newsitem.title: UK: London gold drops sharply to near four-year lows.
newsitem.headline: London gold drops sharply to near four-year lows.

text.p: Gold prices eroded to near four year lows on Friday, dipping dangerously below the $340 an ounce target for a time in a single-mindedly bearish market.
Bullion fixed at $339.75 in the afternoon, down $1.25 from the morning's level and nearly $3.00 off from Thursday's London close. Both fixings were lows since April 22, 1993.
"The funds have gold on the run. It's really going to have to struggle to get out of this," a dealer said.
Prices had threatened to sink towards the eventual target of $330 an ounce before finding footing back above $340.00.
Technical analysts said indicators and price movements suggested gold would bounce moderately in the very near future before resuming the months-old decline.
Silver, in contrast, moved sharply higher in a speculative shortcovering rally after initially sinking with gold to the $4.80 support level.
It was quoted 11 cents stronger at $4.93/$4.95, but off the day's high of $4.97.

"Yet again we see silver being sold down, then covering. Gold is in a true bear market, but there is no rhyme or reason to sell silver," a dealer said. "Once it got down to $4.80 and stopped there people started covering. But at $4.95-$5.00 it ran into more selling."

Palladium was also stronger, reaching itshighest level in six months as users of the metal and speculators raided the spot market to counter shortages created by delayed 1997 export shipments from Russia to Japan, the main user of the metal.
Palladium was fixed at $130.50 in the morning and afternoon, $1.50 up since Thursday.
Its sister metal platinum, which has been under pressure from gold's weakness was $1.25 easier at $350.00/$351.00.
Gold prices have been deteriorating for a year since they fixed at $416.25 in February 2 last year.
But the trend accelerated since the middle of last year as gold producers stepped up selling to protect their income against falling prices.
At the same time, the suspicion grew that the central banks and other financial institutions were mulling selling gold from their reserves.

"The factors for gold are the same as we have seen all year but I am more convinced that central banks have been in the market and selling," a dealer said, adding that gold producers were still hedging to protect themselves against falling prices.
